title: How to build data analysis problems to solve for your portfolio on Mac
metaTitle: Data Analysis Problems to Solve: Portfolio Building Guide for Mac Users
description: Struggling to find data analysis problems to solve for your portfolio? Learn how to build job-ready projects on your Mac without generic datasets.
intro: Finding unique data analysis problems to solve is the biggest hurdle for analysts building a portfolio. You need to move beyond standard tutorials to show hiring managers how you think.
tldr: Stop using generic datasets like Titanic or Iris.
Focus on business questions, not just technical skills.
Document your cleaning process to show you can handle messy data.
Aim for 3 to 5 high-quality, end-to-end projects.
Use your Mac to manage your workflow with tools like DBeaver and JupyterLab.

blocks.text: Why finding data analysis problems to solve is hard

Many analysts get stuck because they think a portfolio is about showing off code. It is actually about showing off business impact. You likely spend too much time on the visual output and not enough on the messy middle of data cleaning. Hiring managers see generic projects and assume you cannot handle real-world ambiguity.

Using datasets found in every bootcamp signals that you are a beginner. It makes your work invisible to recruiters who see hundreds of identical submissions. You lose the chance to demonstrate that you can define a problem, find your own data, and clean it for analysis.
How to fix your portfolio approach

items: Find a real job description and extract a core business question.
Use public data sources to answer that specific question.
Document every step of your cleaning process in a README file.
Focus on the methodology rather than just the final dashboard.
Keep your project count low but your depth high.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you build your portfolio

Lazur helps you maintain focus while you work on your data projects. It acts as a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. You can ask it to explain complex concepts or guide you through tool setups without leaving your workspace.

faq.question: How many projects should be in my portfolio?
faq.answer: Experts recommend 3 to 5 deeply documented projects. Quality is more important than quantity.

faq.question: Can I use Excel for my data analysis projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Excel is standard for quick data verification and sharing, even if you use Python for the heavy lifting.

faq.question: Do I need a paid tool to build a good portfolio?
faq.answer: No. Most tools like DBeaver, JupyterLab, and Tableau Public are free for individuals.
